exposure: Maternal body mass index (BMI) category (non-obese at pre-pregnancy and delivery, non-obese at pre-pregnancy but obese at delivery, obese at pre-pregnancy and delivery)
outcome: Maternal serum total thiol (SH + SS) levels
Maternal thiol-disulfide ratios (SS/SH, SS/total thiol, and SH/total thiol)
Fetal cord blood SH + SS levels
cohort: The study included 125 healthy pregnant women aged over 18 years, between 37 and 41 weeks of gestation, who had not used medications other than iron and folic acid, and whose newborns had birth weights between 2,500 g and 4,500 g with Apgar scores >= 7 at 5 minutes.
finding: Maternal obesity, whether pre-existing or developed during pregnancy, was associated with significantly lower maternal serum native thiol and total thiol levels, indicating disrupted dynamic thiol-disulfide homeostasis and reduced antioxidant capacity, though no significant differences were found in fetal cord blood parameters.
